name: Application of Remote Sensing and GIS in Engineering

units.title: FUNDAMENTALS OF REMOTE SENSING
topics: components, and role in multidisciplinary applications.  Types of Remote Sensing: Active and Passive systems with real-world examples (weather radar
satellite imaging).  Electromagnetic Spectrum: Basic concepts and relevance in environmental monitoring
imaging systems, and sensor design.  Interaction of EMR with Atmosphere: Scattering
atmospheric windows and implications for weather
climate, and communication systems.  Interaction of EMR with Earth’s Surface: Spectral signatures of natural and built features (vegetation
urban areas).  Introduction to freely available satellite data and platforms (Bhuvan
Copernicus).  Basic visual interpretation using tools like Google Earth

units.title: REMOTE SENSING DATA PRODUCTS
topics:  Types and classification of remote sensing data products (optical
radiometric, and temporal resolutions.  Freely available RS datasets: Bhuvan
Copernicus Open Access Hub.  Overview of modern satellite missions (e.g.
Landsat).  Introduction to UAV/Drone-based remote sensing and its applications.  Data formats

units.title: INTRODUCTION TO GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEM
topics:  Definition and scope of GIS in multidisciplinary applications (engineering
environment, IT, business analytics).  Components of GIS (hardware
people).  Spatial vs Non-spatial data and their integration.  Data input/output methods (manual, GPS, remote sensing
KML).  Coordinate systems and map projections
georeferencing concepts.  Introduction to spatial data infrastructure and open data ecosystems
Program Name: Bachelor of Engineering Level: UG Branch: ALL (Except Civil Engineering and Allied Branches) Subject Code: BE05000441 Subject Name: Application of RS and GIS in Engineering

units.title: RS-GIS SOFTWARE AND OPEN PLATFORMS
topics:  Overview of GIS and image processing software (QGIS

Google Earth Engine).  Capabilities and limitations of open-source vs commercial tools.  Data management and visualization in GIS platforms.  Spatial data models: Raster and Vector.  Attribute data management and database basics.  Open GIS data sources: OpenStreetMap
SW Maps) and field data collection.  Introduction to Web GIS and cloud-based geospatial platforms

units.title: IMAGE INTERPRETATION AND DIGITAL IMAGE PROCESSING
topics: image formats, and visualization.  Visual interpretation techniques: tone
association using tools like Google Earth.  Image processing techniques: NDVI
change detection.  Image enhancement: contrast stretching
band combinations.  Image rectification and restoration.  Introduction to AI/ML-based classification concepts (non- mathematical overview)

units.title: GIS SPATIAL DATA ANALYSIS
topics:  Spatial and non-spatial data operations in GIS.  Raster vs Vector analysis in QGIS.  Terrain analysis using DEM: slope
drainage network.  Introduction to Python in GIS (conceptual exposure for IT/AI students).  Use of GIS plugins and processing tools.  Basics of spatial modeling and decision support systems

units.title: APPLICATION OF REMOTE SENSING & GIS
topics: urban analytics, and infrastructure planning.  Climate change monitoring and sustainability assessment.  Disaster management: floods
earthquakes (real-time monitoring).  Agriculture and environmental applications (crop monitoring
deforestation).  Introduction to Web-GIS and geospatial dashboards.  Case studies using free datasets (Bhuvan flood maps
